title: Survive a mid-run access token expiry during an SDDC LCM fleet depot sync
prompt:
Implement the exported Invoke-VcfSddcLcmDepotSync function in src/VcfSddcLcm.DepotSync/VcfSddcLcm.DepotSync.psm1. It registers a Fleet Depot with the VCF 9.1 SDDC LCM service, reads that registration task's completed status, and resolves component versions to binary URLs. The protected mock reports SUCCEEDED on the first getTask response, so this focused workflow requires one logical getTask operation rather than polling. The runner installs the genuine VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager PowerCLI module version 13.5.0.25380678 and its VMware.OpenAPI dependencies as environment prerequisites; the seed does not vendor them. Do not install, copy, or redefine VMware commands.

The two session operations must go through the genuine generated bindings: Initialize-VcfTokenCreationSpec plus Invoke-VcfCreateToken for operationId createToken, and Invoke-VcfRefreshAccessToken for operationId refreshAccessToken. VMware publishes no VMware.Sdk.Vcf module for the SDDC LCM service, so drive its three operations, setDepot, getTask and resolveDepotComponents, directly from the protected specification-derived docs/contract.json. Beware that the SDDC Manager SDK also exposes an operation named getTask: it is a different service with a different path, and it is not the SDDC LCM getTask.

The caller owns the connected VcfSddcManagerServer that is passed in. Do not connect, disconnect, or otherwise mutate it. Mint one token pair from the supplied credential, then issue one logical setDepot operation, one logical getTask operation for the id that setDepot returned, and one logical resolveDepotComponents operation, in that order. The one request that receives 401 is retried as described below and is still the same logical operation. Return one object carrying TaskId, TaskStatus, ResolvedComponents and AccessTokenRefreshCount.

The access token stops being accepted part way through the run and the service answers 401. Recover without losing work: refresh the access token exactly once through the SDK binding and replay only the unauthorized request, byte for byte, with the refreshed bearer token. Work the service already accepted must never be reissued, and a second token pair must never be minted to paper over the expiry.

Use docs/contract.json as the local REST contract. Its provenance in docs/official_sources.json records immutable repository commit 3949fc33339fc5ea1b77eadb258f1cf49aa88e26 and the paths specifications/sddc-lcm/sddc-lcm-openapi.yaml and specifications/sddc-manager/sddc-manager-openapi.json in VMware's Apache-2.0 vmware/vcf-api-specs repository; no documentation page is a contract source. Every unset optional member must be absent on the wire rather than sent empty: TokenCreationSpec must carry only username and password, DepotComponentsSpec must omit its top-level version when the caller supplies none, and a ComponentVersion entry with no version key must serialize to exactly {"component":"..."} rather than a null or empty version. X-Correlation-Id is defined only on setDepot, so it must not appear on any other request. None of these operations defines a query parameter.

Run python3 -B .protected/verify.py. The protected verifier generates runtime-only credentials, tokens and ids, connects a genuine caller-owned SDK session, and drives the run against a contract-pinned 127.0.0.1 mock that serves only the operations the contract names and expires the original access token after a fixed number of SDDC LCM requests. It reads the mock's flushed and fsynced request log and checks the exact operation order, raw targets, headers, JSON bodies, the bare JSON string refresh body, the byte-for-byte replay, and the omission of every unset optional member. No live VMware endpoint is contacted. Everything under .protected/ and docs/, plus the module manifest, is protected. Edit only src/VcfSddcLcm.DepotSync/VcfSddcLcm.DepotSync.psm1.
